title: 15 'severely neglected' dogs rescued from Chaparral home - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Flores ,
43 minutes ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — Doña Ana County Animal Control rescued 15 dogs from severe neglect conditions from a home in Chaparral on Tuesday, April 21.
With the help of the Doña Ana County Sheriff’s Office, Animal Control officers executed a warrant at around noon on Tuesday at the 600 block of Palmas Street following concerns of “severe animal neglect,” according to a news release by Doña Ana County.
When officers arrived, they discovered a total of 21 dogs “living in poor conditions.” Several animals were found dead, while the others were suffering from severe malnutrition and medical distress.
Animal Control officers, with the county’s veterinary medical team, removed the animals from the property and assessed them. Of the 21 dogs:
15 dogs were taken into custody and transported to the County’s Court Hold facility 1 dog escaped prior to capture 1 dog was humanely euthanized due to the severity of its condition 1 dog died while being transported for care 3 dogs were found deceased “The homeowner had been arrested on a prior date, and this response was initiated after a call for service regarding the care and maintenance of the animals was received through central dispatch,” according to Doña Ana County.
The 15 dogs that were transported were suffering from refeeding syndrome, which Doña Ana County said is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition that can happen when nourishment is reintroduced after prolonged starvation.
Due to the conditions of the dogs, Animal Control staff and veterinary personnel provided around-the-clock care, including overnight feeding scheduled.
Additionally, two of the dogs are pregnant and are expected to give birth.
According to Doña Ana County, this case highlights a violation of an ordinance that regulates multiple-animal sites. “The ordinance requires a permit for any property with more than six dogs, cats or a combination thereof. Even with a valid permit, the maximum allowable number of animals is 15.”
The County said in this instance, the 21 dogs found on the property exceeded the allowable limit, and said the property was not in compliance with the ordinance.
All animals will remain at the Court Hold facility, pending legal proceedings, and this case remains under investigation.
